requirement: Collection failure cannot become a complete successful measurement

primary_realization.note: The concrete, real-tool realization of this requirement is F008: gd-tools 0.4.0's own gdtoolkit-based parser rejects a legitimate engine-valid file (UTF-8 BOM prefix), and the resulting CoveragePlan silently omits it with no durable record. See oracles/F008.json for the measured evidence. This requirement therefore already has a verified failing case against a real tool, not just a synthetic one.

harness_synthetic_control.note: Independent of any specific tool, pilot/harness/faults.py provides a generic fault-injection primitive (make_unwritable) so this requirement can be tested against future adapters that use a write-based instrumentation strategy, not just gd-tools' parse-based one.
harness_synthetic_control.mechanism: chmod a fixture source file to read-only, then attempt to write instrumented content to it
harness_synthetic_control.harness_requirement: An adapter wrapper that catches this write failure must report the affected file as failed/excluded in its own structured outcome record (see pilot/harness/comparator.py's missing_files handling), never as a silent success or a false zero.

notes: This case is intentionally satisfied two ways: by an already-real finding against gd-tools (F008), and by a generic, tool-independent fault-injection primitive in the harness for use against later adapters (Nano Coverage, godot-code-coverage) that may fail via a different mechanism than a second parser. No fixture-specific GDScript files are needed here beyond F008's.

ambiguities: If a future adapter's instrumentation writes to a NEW file rather than overwriting the original (e.g. writing to a build/cache directory), make_unwritable on the source file won't trigger a failure the same way; a make_dir_unwritable variant targeting the adapter's actual output path would be needed then.
